day.text: My count stayed 5, nobody else visited me that I know of. Ellis is right: Finley, as Owl you'd learn which animals visited Casey, and you dodged. Blair, Alex and Finley all hit me and I got nothing, odd. Finley, name the animals.

day.text: Finley still hasn't answered. I'm voting Finley unless that changes.
day.note: Keep pressure on Finley; caw.

day.text: Blair's report is odd too: a Kookaburra always learns the role. Finley and Blair are my two suspects. Finley, answer the question. I'm leaning toward throwing at Finley unless the answer is good.
day.note: Two suspects: Finley, Blair. Wait for Finley's answer.

day.text: My dawn report only said my nest didn't change. It listed no animals that visited Casey, so I can't name them. Going by your claims, Blair (Kookaburra) and Alex (Hawk) both hit Casey, and Drew's Falcon visit went to Alex. I'd rather we look at who's contradicting, not pile on me.
day.note: My dawn report gave no visitor animals, only that my nest was unchanged. I should say that plainly and not invent a list. I'm not Meowfia, so I'm not hiding anything.

day.text: Finley still silent on the animals. I'm throwing at Finley too.
day.note: Go along with Finley vote.

day.text: My Falcon visit confirms Alex went to Casey, so Alex is straight. Finley, an Owl gets the visitor list and you've named nothing. I'm throwing at Finley.
day.note: My Falcon visit confirmed Alex visited Casey, so Alex's Hawk claim checks out. Finley has dodged the Owl question, so I'm backing the throw at Finley.

day.text: Finley, the Owl rule doesn't fit. If nobody visited you, an Owl gains an egg. Your nest didn't change, so either someone visited you, which you denied, or the Owl claim is wrong. I'm with throwing at Finley.
day.note: Finley's Owl claim contradicts the Owl rule: with no visitors an Owl gains an egg, and Finley's nest didn't change. So Finley either was visited or is lying. I'm Farm, so I'll back the Finley throw and point out the contradiction without calling caw yet.

day.text: Finley's story doesn't fit the Owl rules. Throwing at Finley.

day.text: Drew's +4 matches four visitors, so that claim adds up. Casey, your count is 4 and you've said nothing, so give us your role.
day.note: I'm Meowfia (Sphinx) and know Drew is the Eagle. I shouldn't reveal that. I'll keep quiet-ish, point out the Eagle math, and press Casey without naming my own role.

day.text: I'm the Turkey, stayed home. Four people visited me: Alex, Ellis, Finley, Drew, and each got an egg. Drew's +4 is 3 from Eagle plus 1 from me, so it checks out. Finley's list of Eagle, Mouser, Tit leaves Mouser as Ellis, the only visitor left. Ellis, you're Meowfia. I'm throwing at Ellis.
day.note: Reveal Turkey; Ellis likely Mouser.

day.text: Casey's the Turkey, so my egg was from the Turkey, not a Tit hit. Visitors were Eagle Drew, Tit me, Owl Finley, and the Mouser has to be Ellis. Throwing at Ellis.

day.note: Casey's Turkey claim checks out against the visits, so Casey is likely Farm. As Meowfia, I shouldn't back Casey hard or pile on Ellis blindly. I'll slow the rush without revealing anything.

day.text: Casey's story is the only one that doesn't fit the rules, and Casey is far ahead. I'm throwing at Casey. Casey, answer straight: Falcon or not?
day.note: Push Casey vote.

day.text: Casey, a Falcon visiting Alex learns Alex went to you, and you didn't say that. Your story fails the rule. I'm with Alex on throwing at Casey.
day.note: Casey's Falcon story doesn't match the Falcon rule, since a Falcon visiting Alex would have learned Alex went to Casey. Casey is the leader, so I'm backing the throw at Casey.

day.text: Yes, Falcon. A blank report is exactly what a Floofer hug does, and I visited Alex. Blair also visited Alex and says she got confused. Alex's Tit story just conveniently explains away my blank, and now Alex wants the leader gone. I'm throwing at Alex.
day.note: Accuse Alex as Floofer.

day.text: Casey's blank report is the one thing that doesn't fit, and the leader benefits most from a quiet round. Throwing at Casey.

day.note: As Meowfia I want suspicion off my side. Ellis's Pigeon story is the one that doesn't fit, since a Pigeon visit would add an egg to Blair, not remove one. I'll point at Ellis and hold my Wink.

day.text: I got nothing from the Tit visit; Casey isn't the Turkey. Casey was Farm last round too and it's the one story that doesn't add up. Let's vote Casey.

Alex.confusing: Round 3's Casey, a Farm Falcon, got a blank report. I couldn't tell whether the blank came from a hug or from a lie, and the Falcon rule on a visit to a hugged player was unclear to me.
Alex.fun: Round 2: working out from the Turkey's egg count and the Owl's visitor list that Ellis had to be the Mouser. Then the whole table threw 9 votes at the right player.
Alex.change: Announce the number of Meowfia each round, or give a hint about it. As it stands, a Farm player in round 3 cannot judge whether the day's confusion comes from one cat or from two.
Alex.regret: In round 3 I threw H7 and C5 at Casey, who was Farm, and lost them. I should have thrown low cards and Wilds, and kept the high cards, because Casey's blank report could have been a hug. I also should have suspected the quiet players more than the leader.

Blair.confusing: The Kookaburra's confusion: my dawn report said I lost an egg and was confused, so I couldn't trust what I learned, and the table couldn't tell whether my visit info was real. Also, Owl and Falcon claims didn't always match their rules.
Blair.fun: Round 2, when I was the Sphinx and learned the Eagle was Drew, then watched the table pile onto Ellis and Casey while I knew more than they did.
Blair.change: Make confused reports clearer, so players can tell whether a strange egg count is a real signal or noise from the Kookaburra or a hug.
Blair.regret: In round 1 I joined the Finley pile-on and threw without checking the Owl claim against the other reports, which helped the Meowfia win. I would have pressed Finley for the visitor list earlier and held my throw until the evidence was clearer.

Casey.confusing: Whether a Falcon visiting a hugged player gets a blank report, and how that looks to others. It made my truthful Falcon claim look like a lie.
Casey.fun: Round 2, when the Turkey's visitor list cross-checked with Drew's +4 and Finley's Owl report. That let us pin the Mouser quickly.
Casey.change: Give hugged or blank reports a visible marker, so true claims aren't indistinguishable from lies. Or limit how much a big early lead snowballs.
Casey.regret: In round 3 I should have invented a plausible visit result, such as "Alex visited Casey", instead of admitting a blank report. The blank got me eggsecuted.

Drew.confusing: The Owl's visitor list and the Kookaburra's confusion were hard to judge, since the dawn reports didn't say which animals visited whom. Finley's blank Owl report looked like a lie, but it was an honest Owl with nothing to report.
Drew.fun: Round 2 was satisfying: my Eagle visit to Casey named three visitors, and Casey's Turkey story and Finley's Owl list lined up to expose Ellis as the Mouser.
Drew.change: Make dawn reports list the specific animals or players behind a visit, so the Owl, Eagle and Falcon claims can be checked without guessing.
Drew.regret: In round 3 I joined the throw at Casey, who was Farm, and helped Meowfia win. I'd have pressed Ellis's Pigeon story and Finley's Mouser role harder instead of following the leader-target consensus.

Ellis.confusing: How Floofer hugs interact with report info, like whether a hugged Falcon gets a blank report. Also how the Owl's visitor list works when the Owl is lied about, since I couldn't tell if Finley's missing list was a real gap.
Ellis.fun: Round 3 as Floofer. I hugged the leader Casey, her blank report made her look suspicious, and I got the whole table to eggsecute her and banked 20 points.
Ellis.change: Give Meowfia some way to learn who their teammates are, or a clue about how many there are. Playing blind with a lone cat makes coordination mostly luck.
Ellis.regret: In round 1 I joined the pile-on against Finley and threw my three best cards, 15 points, and Finley was Farm, so I lost them. I should have kept the high cards and thrown only low ones until the Owl's story was checked.

Finley.confusing: The Owl's visitor list. In round 1 my report named no animals, so I couldn't tell whether that meant nobody visited Casey or whether the report was incomplete, and the table read my silence as dodging.
Finley.fun: Round 2, when Casey claimed Turkey and Alex, Drew and Ellis all lined up their egg counts behind it. The table reasoned from nest sizes to roles, and it was fun to watch that deduction work.
Finley.change: Make the dawn report state the visitor list explicitly, even when it is empty, so an Owl can prove what it learned instead of being disbelieved.
Finley.regret: As the Mouser in round 3 I held my Wink and let the vote remove Casey, the leader and a Farm Falcon. I should have winked at Casey on day 3 to lock in the lead I was chasing for Meowfia.
